en: The Jātaka,
Great Section (Mahānipāta),
Chapter on the Blind-born (Mūgapakkhavagga)
4. The Nimijātaka:
"How wonderful indeed it is in this world that those who possess true insight arise!"
When King Nimi was wise and seeking what is wholesome,
he was the king of all the Videhas.
The subduer of enemies gave a gift;
as he was giving that gift,
a resolution arose within him.
Between giving and the holy life,
which yields the greater fruit?
Having understood his intention, [the Buddha spoke].
Maghavā, the elephant among gods,
thousand-eyed, has appeared,
dispelling the darkness with his radiance.
Nimi, the lord of men, spoke to Vāsava:
"Are you a deity, or are you a gandhabba?"
"Or even Śakra Purindada.
Yet such a complexion as yours has never been seen or heard of by me."
"Tell me, venerable sir,
how we may know you. Having recognized him with his hair standing on end, [he said:]
Vāsava said to Nimi:
“I am Sakka, the lord of the gods;
I have come into your presence.”
“O Lord of Men, Alomahaṭṭha,
ask whatever question you desire. Having been granted leave by him, he spoke.
Nimi said to Vāsava:
“I ask you, O Great King,
Lord of all beings.”
"Between almsgiving and the holy life,
which one bears greater fruit?
Thus was he questioned by the God among Men.
Vāsava spoke to Nimi:
"Knowing the fruit of the holy life,
you have declared it to one who knows."
“By an inferior holy life one is reborn among the Khattiyas;
by a middling one, one attains the state of a deva.”
One is purified by the highest [practice].
These bodies are not easily obtained by anyone through mere begging.
Those who are born in the body,
homeless ascetics—
like a lamp on a crag by the ocean.
Mujakinda, Bhagīrasa,
Usindara, Kassapa, Asaka,
and the worldling Puthujjana.
These and many other kings, kshatriyas, and brahmins,
having performed various sacrifices, [attained their respective realms].
They did not transcend the state of being a mere creature.
Then there were those who lived as homeless ascetics.
Sattisaya, Yāmahanu,
Somayāma, Manojava,
Samudda, Māgha, and Bharata.
Isi was honored by Kāla;
so too were Aṅgīrasa, Kassapa,
Kisavaccha, and Akatti.
To the north flows the Sīdā River,
deep and difficult to cross;
its reed-tipped waters gleam with light.
The mountains were always like mountains of gold;
the thickets were overgrown with *tagara*,
and the forests and trees were lush and flourishing.
There, in former times, were ten thousand ancient seers;
I was the best among them in generosity.
Through self-restraint and self-control,
having performed the supreme vow,
he wandered about, concentrated in mind.
I shall pay homage beyond measure to that upright man who is noble by birth yet free from pride.
For young men are bound by their actions;
all castes that stand in unrighteousness fall down into hell.
"All castes are purified by practicing the supreme Dhamma.
Having said this, Maghavā—
Sujampati, the king of the gods,
having instructed the people of Videha,
departed for the heavenly realm.
“Pay attention to this, sirs,
as many as are gathered here:
[the teaching] of righteous men.”
Much varied praise was given,
such as this: "This King Nimi is wise and seeks what is skillful."
The King, the subduer of enemies,
gave gifts to all the people of Videha. As he was giving that gift,
The thought arose in him:
"Between giving and the holy life,
which is of greater fruit?"
“Truly wonderful in the world has arisen that which makes the hair stand on end;
a divine chariot has appeared.”
Of the illustrious King of Videha.
Mātali, the divine charioteer, possessed of great supernormal power, was a son of the gods.
They invited the king,
the Videhan from Mithilā:
"Come, mount this chariot."
O best of kings, Disampati:
the gods of the Tāvatiṃsa realm, together with Indra, desire to see you.
"Indeed, the gods are eager for you;
they are waiting in the Sudhamma hall.
Then the king, hurrying, [went there].
Videha, the lord of Mithilā,
rose from his seat and,
facing forward, ascended the chariot.
Having ascended the divine chariot,
Mātali said this:
"By which path shall I lead you?"
"O best of kings, Disampati:
by what [means] do men become those of evil deeds or those of meritorious deeds?"
“Take me by both means,
Mātali, divine charioteer:
either to where those of evil deeds [dwell],”
"And those men who have performed meritorious deeds.
"By what means, O best of kings, Disampati, do I lead you first?"
"Or by whom are those people of evil deeds and those people of meritorious deeds [known]?
"First, I see them in hell."
In the dwelling of those who commit evil deeds,
the place of those who perform cruel acts,
and the destination of those who are immoral.”
Mātali showed the King the difficult-to-cross river Vetaraṇī,
boiling and filled with caustic salt water.
The truth is like a flame of fire.
Having seen people falling into a difficult-to-cross abyss, Nimī indeed spoke thus to Mātali.
“Fear indeed comes upon me, O charioteer, upon seeing these;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:
what evil have these mortals committed?”
“Which people fall into the Vaitaraṇī River?
Being thus questioned, Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, replied:
Knowing the ripening of evil deeds,
speak as one who knows:
"In this world of living beings, those who are weak are overcome by the strong."
Those of very evil nature who injure and provoke others,
having accumulated that evil through their cruel deeds,
those people fall into the Vetaraṇī River.
“Hawks, owls, vultures,
and terrifying flocks of crows devour me;
O charioteer, seeing this, fear has come upon me.”
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals done,
that these hosts of crows devour them?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil kamma.
One who knows should declare it to one who knows:
"Whosoever among these are miserly and stingy,
who revile ascetics and brahmins..."
Those of very evil nature who harm and provoke others,
having committed cruel deeds and produced evil,
those people are devoured by flocks of crows.
“Blazing with fire, they tread upon the earth and strike me with their burning bodies;
O charioteer, fear indeed comes over me upon seeing this.”
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals done,
that these people lie here, their limbs shattered?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil kamma.
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"Those in this world of the living who are of very evil character,
yet [claim] both men and women to be of non-evil character;"
Those of very evil nature who harm and provoke others,
having committed wicked deeds through their cruel actions—
those people lie down, struck down by the mass of their own karma.
“Others are throwing [the man] into a pit of glowing coals;
the men, weeping, have their limbs scorched.
O charioteer, fear indeed comes upon me upon seeing this.”
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals committed,
that these people are scattering burning coals upon them?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil karmas.
One who knows should declare it to one who knows:
"Whatever groups, for the sake of wealth, cause a debt to be paid by taking someone as a witness; [they all go to hell]."
Having caused those people to gamble, O Lord of Men,
and having made them commit cruel deeds and produce evil,
those people then pour [the ashes] into a pit of glowing coals.
“Blazing, flaming, and glowing,
a great iron cauldron shines forth;
O charioteer, fear indeed comes upon me upon seeing it.”
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals done,
that these people fall headfirst into the iron cauldron?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil deeds.
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"Those of very evil nature who harm and provoke a virtuous ascetic or brahmin..."
Having brought forth that evil through their cruel deeds,
those people fall head-first into the iron cauldron.
They tear out their necks after having wrapped them [in cloth].
Having sprinkled it with hot water,
O charioteer, fear has come upon me at the sight of it;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer.
"What evil have these mortals done,
that these people lie here with their heads shorn?
Being thus questioned, he replied:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of evil kamma,
spoke to one who already knew.
“Those of very evil nature in this world of living beings seize birds and torment them;
having tormented the bird, O Lord of Men...”
Having committed those deeds of cruelty and produced evil,
those people lie with their heads shorn.
[The rivers] abound with water and have unfathomable banks.
This river flows with a firm foundation;
men, tormented by the heat, drink from it,
and for them, that water becomes a great refreshment.
"Indeed, fear seizes me upon seeing this, O charioteer;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:
what evil have these mortals committed?"
"And their drink becomes turbid.
Thus questioned, Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, replied.
Knowing the ripening of evil deeds,
speak as one who knows:
"Those who mix pure grain with chaff..."
Those who perform impure deeds give to those who are tormented by heat and parched with thirst; yet for them,
that water becomes like dregs when drunk.
"With arrows, spears, and javelins,
they strike at both sides as I cry out;
for fear seizes me, O charioteer, upon seeing this."
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil did these mortals commit,
that these people lie here slain by swords?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil kamma:
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"Those in the world of the living who perform unwholesome deeds,
they make their livelihood by taking what is not given."
Grain, wealth, silver, and gold,
goats, sheep, cattle, and buffaloes—
having produced such evil through their cruel deeds, they [reap the consequences].
“People lie down terrified, struck by swords.
Why are these others bound by the neck?
And why do yet others lie down, cut to pieces and mangled?”
For fear seizes me, O charioteer, upon seeing this;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:
what evil have these mortals committed?
“People eat and lie down in the same place.
Thus questioned, Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, replied.
Knowing the ripening of evil deeds,
speak as one who knows:
"The slaughterers of sheep, the slaughterers of pigs, and the fishers..."
Having slaughtered cattle, buffalo, goats, and sheep,
they stretched them out upon the spits; those hunters,
having committed that evil deed, brought forth their own sin.
People tremble and lie down in fear.
‘This lake is filled with urine and excrement;
it is foul-smelling, impure, and reeks of putrefaction.’”
"Men devoted to God eat [this],
for fear seizes me upon seeing it, O Sūta;
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods."
"What evil deed have these mortals done,
that these people must feed upon urine and excrement?
Being thus questioned, he replied:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of evil kamma,
spoke thus to one who knew.
“Whosoever these litigants and quarrelers may be,
who are ever intent on harming others;
having produced evil through their cruel deeds, they shall experience its fruit.”
The fools who eat filth are those who take what is not given.
This lake is filled with blood and pus;
it is foul-smelling, impure, and reeks of putrefaction.
"Afflicted by the heat, these humans drink;
for fear seizes me upon seeing them, O Sūta.
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:"
"What evil deed have these mortals done,
that these people here subsist on blood and pus?
Being thus questioned, he explained:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of evil kamma,
spoke to one who knew.
“Those who, in this world of the living, commit a pārājika offense against their mother or father, or kill an arahant—
having performed such cruel deeds and produced evil, they [fall into hell].”
“People tremble, those who feed on blood and pus.
“Behold the tongue pierced by the hook,
like hide struck by a hundred spears.”
"Like young fish cast upon the dry land, they writhe and shed tears while weeping; why is this?
O charioteer, fear seizes me as I behold them."
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals done,
that these people lie here with their hands twisted?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil kamma.
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"Whosoever among men have entered into partnership,
they diminish the value of their purchase by means of its price."
Out of greed for wealth, one person deceives another with deception,
just as a fisherman conceals his snare to kill a water-dweller.
For there is no protection for the deceiver.
Those people who, surrounded by their own deeds,
have committed cruel acts and produced evil,
lie down with their hands bound behind their backs.
“These women of low birth, their limbs mangled,
are crying out as they clutch my arms;
they are smeared and drenched in blood and pus.”
Just as oxen slaughtered at the place of execution are always impaled upon stakes in the ground,
so do these trunks pass by, set ablaze with fire.
Indeed, fear seizes me, O charioteer, upon seeing this;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:
what evil did these women commit?
“That which is always buried in the ground—
its flames blaze forth, transcending the trunk.
Being thus questioned, he replied:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of evil deeds,
spoke to one who already knew.
“O women of Kolita, in this world of the living,
those of impure deeds who act unrighteously and improperly— though they possess beautiful forms—
they, having abandoned their husbands, [fall away].”
For the sake of pleasure and sport, they engage in other improper acts;
having caused delight in this world of the living,
they pass beyond the aggregates like blazing fires.
“Having seized them by the feet,
why do these others throw them headlong into hell?
For fear seizes me, O charioteer, upon seeing this.”
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What evil have these mortals done,
that these people cause them to fall headlong into hell?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil kamma.
One who knows should declare it to one who knows:
"Those in this world of the living who perform unwholesome deeds and transgress against the wives of others..."
Such as they are, those thieves of the most excellent goods—
those people, with their heads cast down, cause themselves to fall into hell;
for many a succession of years they remain there.
In the hells, they experience painful sensations;
for one who has committed evil deeds, there is no refuge when he is confronted by his own actions.
“Having committed those cruel deeds and produced evil,
those people, with their heads hanging down, cause themselves to fall into hell.
“Various and manifold are the means employed,”
"Terrible forms are seen in the hells;
indeed, O charioteer, fear seizes me upon seeing them.
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:"
"What evil deed have these mortals done,
that these people now experience such excessive,
sharp, harsh, and bitter sensations?"
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of evil deeds.
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"Those in the world of the living who hold very evil views perform acts of trust out of delusion."
Moreover, they incite others toward wrong views;
having generated evil through their wicked views,
those people experience excessive, sharp, and piercing suffering.
“They experience harsh and bitter sensations.
“Great King, you have recognized the dwelling place of those who commit evil deeds.”
The states of those who commit cruel deeds and the destiny of the immoral—
now depart from here, O King!
In the presence of the king of the gods,
this five-storied celestial mansion is seen,
with garlands and wreaths suspended in the midst of the bed.
"There dwells a woman of great majesty,
performing various transformations of psychic power through her supernormal abilities.
"O charioteer, upon seeing her, a sense of wonder has indeed come over me."
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What good deed did this woman perform,
that she rejoices, having attained heaven, in a celestial mansion?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of meritorious deeds.
One who knows should speak to one who knows:
"If you have heard, O hero, that in the world of the living there was a slave girl named Āmāyā belonging to a brahmin..."
Recognizing a guest when the time was right,
she rejoiced in him as a mother does in her son;
she was self-restrained and generous.
She rejoices in that celestial mansion.
Radiant, they illuminate the seven mansions that have been fashioned.
There a yakkha of great psychic power,
adorned with all kinds of ornaments,
wanders about on every side.
“Surrounded by a host of women.
“Indeed, O Sūta, a sense of wonder has come upon me upon seeing this;
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods.”
"What good deed did this mortal perform,
that he rejoices, having reached heaven in a celestial mansion?
Being thus questioned, he replied:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
spoke to one who knew.
“Thus was the householder Soṇadinna,
this lord of giving;
he went forth for the sake of the Teaching.”
He had seven monasteries built.
He attended upon those monks residing there with great care.
He gave clothing, food, lodgings, and lamps to those who had become upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the lunar fortnight.
And observing the Uposatha on the day of miracles, well-composed in the eight factors.
Always restrained in virtuous conduct,
disciplined and generous,
he rejoices in a celestial mansion.
This celestial mansion shines,
well-fashioned from crystal,
crowded with throngs of the most excellent women.
Adorned with excellent gabled halls,
and provided with both food and drink,
as well as dancing and singing.
“Indeed, O charioteer, a sense of wonder has found me upon seeing this;
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:
What good deed have these mortals performed?”
"Those who have attained heaven rejoice in their celestial mansions.
Thus questioned, Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, gave this explanation.
Knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
speak as one who knows:
"Whatever women there are here in this world of the living..."
The virtuous female lay disciples,
always delighting in giving with a serene mind,
established in truth, and heedful on the Uposatha days;
"Through self-restraint and sharing,
they rejoice in that celestial mansion.
This celestial abode shines forth."
It was fashioned out of beryl;
it was endowed with various grounds,
divided into sections, and measured out with precision.
Āḷambaras and mudiṅgas, dancing,
singing, and beautiful instrumental music—
divine sounds resound.
The offerings were delightful.
Never before have I seen anything so well-prepared or so exceedingly beautiful as this.
I fully understand sound,
whether seen or heard; for, O Sūta,
when I have seen it, a sense of well-being arises within me.
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What good deed did these mortals perform, that they rejoice now,
having reached celestial palaces in heaven?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of meritorious deeds.
One who knows should declare it to one who knows:
"Whatever lay followers there may be here in this world of the living who are virtuous..."
In groves and at wells,
at water-stations and crossroads—
[one should honor] the Arhats who have become cooled.
They respectfully provided robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings.
They gave with a serene mind to those who have become upright,
on the fourteenth and the fifteenth day.
And on the eighth day of the fortnight,
and during the fortnight of miracles, one should be well-composed in the eightfold [precepts].
They observed the Uposatha,
always restrained in their virtuous conduct,
self-controlled and generous.
“They rejoice in that celestial mansion. This palace shines forth,
beautifully constructed of crystal.
Crowded with throngs of excellent women,
adorned with the finest gabled houses,
and provided with food and drink.
With both dance and song;
and rivers flow all around,
filled with various flowering trees.
"O charioteer, having seen him, joy has indeed found me;
therefore, Mātali, divine charioteer, I ask you:
what good deed did this mortal perform?"
“He who rejoices, having reached heaven in a celestial mansion”—
being thus questioned, Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, explained it to him:
Knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
you have declared it to one who understands:
"In Mithilā, O householder..."
This man was a lord of generosity;
he established monasteries and wells,
rest-houses and bridges.
I respectfully provided robes and almsfood for the Arhant who had become cooled.
He gave bedding and seating as a requisite to those who have become upright,
with a mind full of serene confidence.
On the fourteenth and the fifteenth,
and on the eighth day of the fortnight,
as well as during the fortnight of miracles—
One who observes the Uposatha well-composed in its eight factors,
always restrained in moral conduct;
Through self-restraint and sharing,
he rejoices in a celestial mansion.
This celestial abode shines forth.
Well-constructed of crystal,
crowded with throngs of excellent women,
and adorned with the finest gabled chambers.
Endowed with both food and drink,
and with both dance and song,
the rivers flow all around it.
Abounding with various flowering trees: rājāyatana figs, wood-apples,
mangoes, sal trees, and rose-apples.
There are many *tinduka* and *piyāla* trees, always bearing fruit.
O charioteer, upon seeing them, a sense of security comes to me.
I ask you, Mātali, charioteer of the gods:
What good deed did this mortal perform,
that he rejoices, having reached heaven and attained a celestial mansion?
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of meritorious deeds.
Knowing, one should speak to the one who knows:
"In Mithilā, there was this householder,
a lord of giving."
In groves and at wells,
at water-stations and crossroads,
[one should honor] the Arhats who have become cool.
He provided [him] with due respect:
robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings.
He gave with a serene mind to those who had become upright,
on the fourteenth and the fifteenth day.
And the eighth day of the fortnight,
and the fortnight of miracles,
well-composed in the eight factors.
One who observes the Uposatha,
always restrained in moral conduct,
and who is self-controlled and generous—
He rejoices in that celestial mansion. This palace shines forth,
fashioned from beryl.
Endowed with various grounds,
divided into sections and measured out;
there were āḷambaras and mudiṅgas,
With beautiful dancing, singing,
and instrumental music, divine sounds resounded—
worthy of being heard and enchanting to the mind.
Never before have I perceived such a sound, so exceedingly beautiful, as this which has come to me.
Whether seen or even heard, O charioteer, a sense of wonder finds me upon seeing this.
Therefore, Mātali, divine charioteer, I ask you: [what is this?]"
"What good deed did this mortal perform,
that he rejoices, having reached heaven and attained a celestial mansion?
Being thus questioned, he explained:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
spoke to one who already knew.
“In Bārāṇasī, householder,
there was this master of giving;
at the monastery and at the well, [he gave].”
She provided with due care bridges and causeways for the arahants who had attained coolness.
He gave robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings to those who were upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the lunar fortnight.
And observing the Uposatha on the day of miracles, well-composed in the eight factors.
Always restrained in virtuous conduct,
disciplined and generous,
he rejoices in a celestial mansion.
Just as the great sun at its rising becomes crimson,
so too is this celestial mansion.
"O charioteer, having seen this creation of gold,
a sense of wonder has come upon me.
I ask you, Mātali, divine charioteer:"
"What good deed did this mortal perform,
that he rejoices, having reached heaven in a celestial mansion?
Being thus questioned, he explained:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
spoke to one who knew.
“In Sāvatthī, there was a householder,
a lord of giving;
at the monastery and at the well, [he gave].”
She provided with great care bridges and causeways for the arahants who had attained coolness.
He gave robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings to those who were upright.
With a serene mind,
on the fourteenth, the fifteenth,
and the eighth day of the lunar fortnight;
And on the fortnight of miracles,
he observed the Uposatha day, well-composed in its eight factors.
Always restrained in virtuous conduct,
disciplined and generous,
he rejoices in a celestial mansion.
“Many [beings] in the air,
fashioned from gold,
shine forth, resplendent.”
"Like lightning amidst thick clouds,
O Sūta, a sense of rapture finds me upon seeing you.
Therefore, Mātali, charioteer of the gods, I ask you:"
"What indeed did these mortals do that was so good,
that they rejoice, having reached celestial palaces in heaven?
Thus questioned, he replied:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
spoke to one who already knew.
“With faith firmly established,
and with the true Dhamma well-proclaimed,
they have carried out the Teacher’s word.”
In the teaching of the Perfectly Enlightened One;
these are those states,
O King, which you behold.
You have understood, O Great King,
the abode of those who perform evil deeds,
as well as that of those who perform wholesome deeds.
These positions are known to you;
now go forth, O lord of kings,
into the presence of the King of Gods.
The Great King, having resolved upon his divine vehicle drawn by horses yoked in thousands, was traveling along.
Seeing mountains within the ocean,
Addā asked the charioteer,
"What are these mountains called?"
Being questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
explained the ripening of meritorious deeds.
Knowing, one should tell to the knower:
"Sudassana, Karavīka,
Īsadhara, and Yugandhara."
Nemindhara, Vinataka,
Assakaṇṇa, and the lofty Giribrahā—
these are the mountains within the Sīdantara ocean.
“Rising up in succession,
O King, are these dwellings of the Great Kings which you behold.”
“Of many forms, beautiful,
and displaying various wonders;
crowded with those resembling Indra,”
“O charioteer, like one well-guarded from tigers,
my livelihood has been found by me upon seeing this.
Therefore, Mātali, divine charioteer, I ask you.”
"What indeed do they call this gate that is so enchanting,
visible even from afar?
Being thus questioned, he explained to him:
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
spoke thus to one who knows.
“That which they call Citrakūṭa,
the entrance to the king of the gods,
[is on] Mount Sudassana.”
This gateway shines forth;
it displays many forms, beautiful,
and variegated with diverse colors.
O King, one should enter [the city] which is crowded with those resembling Indra and well-guarded like tigers.
I traversed the dustless ground,
established upon a divine vehicle drawn by a thousand horses.
While traveling, O Great King,
he saw this assembly of gods,
like [the stars] in the autumn sky.
A blue radiance is seen;
this celestial mansion is fashioned from beryl, and it is just like that.
"O charioteer, having seen this, joy indeed finds me.
Mātali, divine charioteer, I ask you:
what do they call this celestial mansion?"
"Manorama is seen from afar.
Being thus questioned by him,
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods, replied:
Knowing the ripening of meritorious deeds,
you have declared it to those who seek to know:
"That which they call 'Sudhammā'..."
The assembly hall is seen from afar;
variegated and beautiful with beryl,
it stands well-constructed.
The pillars are well-fashioned with eight facets,
all made of beryl;
there the Tāvatiṃsa gods [dwell].
All the priests of Indra,
contemplating the welfare of gods and humans, strove together.
"O King, enter with the gods' approval. The gods rejoiced in that.
Seeing that the king had arrived, [he said]:
"Welcome to you, Great King;
indeed, it is not ill-timed for you to have come."
“Now sit down, O King of Men,
in the presence of the King of Gods.
Sakka also welcomed him in return.
Vāsava invited the Lord of Videha,
the ruler of Mithilā, with sensual pleasures and a seat.
“Excellent! You have arrived at the abode of those who wield power;
dwell among the gods as their sovereign king.”
"Among the Tāvatiṃsa devas, where all desires are fulfilled,
enjoy superhuman pleasures."
Just as a borrowed vehicle,
just as borrowed wealth—
so too is this attainment.
That which comes from others by way of a gift as a condition—
I do not desire that which comes from others by way of a gift as a condition.
Meritorious deeds performed by myself—
this is my unique wealth.
Having gone among humans, I...
I shall perform much wholesome merit through generosity, righteous conduct,
self-restraint, and self-mastery.
"Having done which one becomes happy and does not regret it later.
"Your honor has been very helpful to us."
Mātali, the charioteer of the gods,
who has shown me the results of both my wholesome and my evil deeds.
Having spoken this, King Nimi,
the ruler of Videha who dwelt in Mithilā,
performed a manifold sacrifice.
"He undertook self-restraint.
This is the fourth Jātaka, the Nimi Jātaka.
